In [[mathematics]], a '''Sylvester domain''', named after [[James Joseph Sylvester]] by {{harvtxt|Dicks|Sontag|1978}},  is a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] in which Sylvester's law of nullity holds. This means that if ''A'' is an ''m'' by ''n'' [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]], and ''B'' is an ''n'' by ''s'' matrix over ''R'', then
:ρ(''AB'') ≥ ρ(''A'') + ρ(''B'') – ''n''
where ρ is the inner rank of a matrix. The inner rank of an ''m'' by ''n'' matrix is the smallest integer ''r'' such that the matrix is a product of an ''m'' by ''r'' matrix and an ''r'' by ''n'' matrix.

{{harvtxt|Sylvester|1884}} showed that [[field (mathematics)|fields]] satisfy Sylvester's law of nullity and are, therefore, Sylvester domains.
